holidays.name: National Cheeseball Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the glorious, round, nut-crusted party appetizer that has anchored snack tables since your grandma's cocktail hour. Break out the crackers and roll up your sleeves!
holidays.origin: Part of the unofficial American food-holiday calendar, popularized by food bloggers and snack enthusiasts. The cheese ball itself surged in popularity in mid-20th-century America as a party staple.
holidays.funFact: In 1801, a giant 1,235-pound cheese ball was reportedly presented to President Thomas Jefferson, a legendary 'Mammoth Cheese' that was actually a wheel from Cheshire, Massachusetts.

holidays.name: Haiku Poetry Day
holidays.description: A day to craft tiny three-line poems in the 5-7-5 syllable pattern. Perfect for people who want to be poetic without committing to a long afternoon.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States and promoted by poetry groups, it honors the Japanese haiku tradition, which developed from the hokku opening verse of linked poems centuries ago.
holidays.funFact: Traditional Japanese haiku do not always follow 5-7-5 in English terms, because Japanese sound units called 'on' are shorter than English syllables.

holidays.name: World Hemophilia Day
holidays.description: An international awareness day dedicated to improving care and access to treatment for people with hemophilia and other inherited bleeding disorders.
holidays.origin: Organized by the World Federation of Hemophilia since 1989, held on April 17 to honor the birthday of its founder, Frank Schnabel.
holidays.funFact: Hemophilia has been nicknamed the 'royal disease' because it affected several descendants of Queen Victoria across European royal families.

holidays.name: Bat Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A celebration of our flappy, nocturnal friends who pollinate plants, gobble up insects, and generally get a bad rap thanks to vampire movies.
holidays.origin: Promoted by conservation groups and wildlife enthusiasts to counter bat myths and highlight their ecological value as pollinators and pest controllers.
holidays.funFact: A single little brown bat can eat up to 1,000 mosquito-sized insects in an hour.

holidays.name: Ellis Island Family History Day
holidays.description: A day for genealogy buffs to dig into family roots and trace ancestors who passed through America's most famous immigration gateway.
holidays.origin: Tied to the heritage of Ellis Island, which processed more than 12 million immigrants between 1892 and 1954. The observance encourages people to research and share their family stories.
holidays.funFact: Contrary to popular legend, officials at Ellis Island generally did not change immigrants' names; most name changes happened later by the immigrants themselves.
